description: Intent i013 (SNAPSHOT=s03, BRANCH=optsize-body-clamp) complete. One reported finding: net/netfilter/xt_dccp.c lines 59-69, dccp_find_option() walks attacker-controlled DCCP header option bytes (fetched via skb_header_pointer into dccp_optbuf at line 53, optlen = dh->dccph_doff*4 - __dccp_hdr_len(dh)) and at line 68 executes "i += op[i+1]?:1" — reading a size byte with no 2-byte-remaining check and no clamp to (optlen - i) — so when the final remaining option byte has value >= 2 the parser reads one byte past the end of the option data (OOB read / adjacent-payload byte leak), exactly the seed mechanism (unvalidated size byte used without size<=remaining guard). Evidence: sibling parser net/netfilter/xt_tcpmss.c line 64 has the explicit guard "if (op[i] < 2 || i == optlen - 1) i++;" which xt_dccp.c lacks. Confidence medium because with a non-linear skb the op pointer is the 1024-byte static dccp_optbuf (line 165) so the extra byte stays inside the allocation, and the walk requires the xt_dccp match rule plus DCCP traffic. All other TCP-family option walkers audited in s03 were verified safe (each has the length<2 plus opsize>length or equivalent guards): tcp_input.c tcp_parse_options:4558, tcp_parse_mss_option:4499, tcp_parse_fastopen_option:4457, smc_parse_options:4475; mptcp/options.c mptcp_get_options:386 (seed fix present); nf_conntrack_proto_tcp.c tcp_options/tcp_sack:366; nf_synproxy_core.c synproxy_parse_options:54; core/filter.c bpf_search_tcp_opt:7740; xt_tcpmss.c:64; xt_TCPOPTSTRIP.c:19 (loop bound i < tcp_hdrlen - 1). Limitations: IPv6 exthdr/TLV, cfg80211/mac80211 IE, Bluetooth EIR/SDP, and SCTP ASCONF walkers in s03 were enumerated but not deeply audited (covered by sibling branch intents); no runtime reproducer compiled. Final artifact written to agent-state/findings/i013.json with snapshots_checked ["s03"], one medium-confidence finding and eleven classified candidates.
